newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks slide on inflation figures.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks slide on inflation figures.

text.p: Mexican stocks slid in late trade on Tuesday due to higher-than-expected inflation figures after the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision to leave interest rates unchanged failed to produce a lasting effect, traders said.
"Inflation was higher than expected. Opinions varied about the (Fed) decision. Some think the Fed did not raise rates for political reasons, so hikes could be larger next time round," a trader said.
The blue chip IPC index closed down 6.85 points, or 0.21 percent, at 3,293.59. Volume was mediocre at 81.8 million shares, but better than on Monday.
"It was nearly all locals who moved the bolsa. Foreign traders were more interested in the U.S. market," the trader added.
The IPC did rise briefly following the Fed decision, but gains soon fizzled as the Dow Jones went into reverse. The inflation figures dampened market enthusiasm further.
Equity analysts expected the Bolsa to continue to move sideways for the rest of the week as dealers awaited reaction to the Fed's decision in the U.S. markets.
"We see no changes in the market's short-term trend. It will stay speculative, nervous and at low volume, while it sees how New York digests the (Fed) decision," an analyst said.

"The only thing that could help us would be positive comments on Mexico by the World Bank or the International Monetary Fund, which could single out winning sectors for the rest of the year," he added.
This situation favoured same-day buy-sell trades in stocks favoured by company news items, traders said.
Holding company Moderna was Tuesday's most-traded stock following news it would sell a U.S. subsidiary, traders said. Moderna gained 10 centavos (1 cent) to close at 37.10 pesos ($4.93).
